Chan Master Sha Bei entered the palace and requested instruction on the Dharma of the mind. The Master said: "Great King, listen with a sincere heart. This illusory and empty body is Your Majesty’s Dharmakāya;
this knowing, seeing, awakening, and understanding is Your Majesty’s own nature (*svabhāva*). When you observe the mind and find no mind, it arises from deluded thoughts.
When one's own mind is naturally empty, one immediately awakens to the true mark (*bhūtalakṣaṇa*). Once the original nature is known, all is attained at once."
"Let it go. Do not give rise to even a hair’s breadth of further thought. The King paid homage to the two masters, saying, "I am fortunate to have encountered such instruction.
The King then asked Xuansha, "This one true mind is fundamentally without birth or extinction; yet this present body—"
From what does it arise? Xuansha said: "This original source, true nature, pervades the entire Dharma-realm.

Because of deluded thoughts, however, a single point of conscious nature arises from the false conditions of father and mother, undergoing a thousand kinds of suffering and subjecting the body to the cycle of rebirth."

The Great King, having thus attained awakening and understanding, shall not fall into the evil realms. I only entreat the Great King to frequently examine his deluded thoughts, so that he may return to truth and harmonize with the Way.
The King prostrated himself and joyfully accepted [the teaching].
King Yanjun was the second son of [Wang] Shenzhi. He had long venerated the Buddha-dharma and ordained ten thousand monks; consequently, there were many monks in Min.
He once invited Master Luoshan to ascend the hall and preach the Dharma. As the master took his place upon the seat, adjusted his robes, and looked around to left and right, [the King] said:
He then descended from his seat. The King stepped forward, took Layman Luoshan by the hand, and said, "How is this assembly on Vulture Peak any different from today?
Luoshan replied, "I thought you were just an ordinary layman. Later, he invited Master Mengbi for a meal. He asked, "Has the Master brought his brush with him?
Mengbi replied, "It is not a brocade-tube pen from Mount Ji; it is ashamed to be anything other than that which dwells within the moon."
"Rabbit fur. "Since Your Majesty has deigned to inquire, how could this mountain monk dare not present [an answer]? He asked again, "What is the Dharma King?
He replied, "It is not the style of the Dream-Pen family."

When Minister Chen arrived at Jiangzhou from Yunmen, there was a certain Minister Chen who invited him for a vegetarian feast. As soon as he saw him, [Minister Chen] asked: "I shall not ask about the Confucian classics;
you have your own masters for the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings. What, then, is the practice of a patch-robed monk?"
[The] matter. Yunmen said, "I have asked several people about this before. The Shangshu replied, "I am asking you, Venerable One, right now.
Yunmen said, "Setting that aside for a moment, what is the meaning of the teachings? The Shangshu replied, "The yellow scrolls and red volumes. Yunmen said:
"This is merely words and language. What is the meaning of the teaching? The Shangshu said, "The mouth wishes to speak, yet words fail;
the mind wishes to contemplate, yet thoughts vanish. Yunmen said, "'The mouth wishes to speak, yet words fail' refers to the presence of speech.
'The mind wishes to contemplate, yet thoughts vanish' refers to the presence of deluded thought. What is the meaning of the teaching? The Shangshu was at a loss.
Yunmen said, "I have heard that you, Minister, study the Lotus Sūtra; is this true? The Minister replied, "It is true. Yunmen said, "The sūtra states:
'All livelihoods and productive enterprises are entirely non-contradictory with the true nature (dharmatā). Now tell me:"
"Not the Heaven of Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception. "How many people have fallen from their positions? The Minister remained silent. Yunmen said, "Minister, do not be so hasty.
Masters of the Three Canons and Five Treatises cast them aside and enter the monastic forests specifically; yet after ten or twenty years, they still cannot manage it.
How could you, Minister, possibly understand? The Minister prostrated and said, "I am at fault."
Vice-Commissioner Wei came to visit Xuansha and said, "The Monk Caoshan is truly extraordinary. Xuansha asked, "How many li is it from Fuzhou to Caoshan?
Vice-Commissioner Wei pointed to a monk standing nearby and asked, "Have you, Venerable Sir, ever been to Caoshan? The monk replied, "I have."
When he arrived, Wei asked, "How many *li* is it from Fuzhou to Caoshan? He replied, "One hundred and twenty *li*.
Wei said, "If that is so, then you, Venerable Sir, have not reached Caoshan. Wei then rose and bowed. Xuansha said, "The Military Inspector ought to bow to this monk;

this monk possesses a sense of shame and remorse. (Yunju Xi said: "Wherein does this monk possess shame and remorse? If you can identify it, I will grant that you, Venerable Sir, have the eye for traveling on pilgrimage. Xuan.
One day, Xuansha was eating pastries with Military Commissioner Wei. Wei asked, "What is it that is used daily yet remains unknown?
Xuansha picked up a pastry and said, "Eat. After Wei had finished eating the pastry, he asked again.
Xuansha said, "This very thing is what is used daily yet remains unknown."
Minister Chen asked Dongshan Jia: "Among the fifty-two stages of the Bodhisattvas, why is the stage of Sublime Enlightenment (Miaojue) not seen?
Dongshan said, "Minister, you have personally seen Sublime Enlightenment."

Cheng Rui, the Regional Inspector (Jiedushi) of Jingnan, entered the mountains to offer a ritual feast and asked Chan Master Yunju Ying, "The World-Honored One had a secret teaching, which Kāśyapa did not conceal.
What is this secret teaching of the World-Honored One? Yunju called out, "Minister! (Shangshu).
The Minister assented. Yunju asked, "Do you understand? The Minister said, "I do not understand.
Yunju said, "If you do not understand, the World-Honored One has a secret teaching; if you do understand, Kāśyapa did not conceal anything."
Liu Yudan asked Chan Master Yunju Deng, "From where does the rain come? Yunju said, "It comes from where you, Official Liu, have asked.
The official was delighted and offered praise. Yunju then asked the official in return, "From where does the rain come? The official was speechless.
An elder monk [once] said on his behalf: "What did you just say? Rourong Guiqing of Guizong replied differently: "I thank the Master for his repeated kindness.
The lay practitioner Zhang Baqian asked Chan Master Kuangren of Shushan: "Master, what words or phrases do you have? Shushan...
Shan presented a verse, saying: "I have a precious lute, which I keep in the wilderness. It is not that I do not know how to play it;
it is simply that I have not yet met a connoisseur."—Liu Weng.
When Chan Master Qinglin Shiqian was planting pine trees at Dongshan, an old man named Liu requested a verse from him. The Master composed a verse, saying:
"More than three feet tall, Lushly covering the green grass. I know not in what generation he lived, Yet he has seen this aged pine.
Upon receiving the verse, Liu presented it to Dongshan. Dongshan remarked, "This is the third-generation master of Dongshan."
One day, while An Tiehu of Zhong Sifu’s Yingqiao was sitting by a brazier in Fengxue, Zhong Sifu came to see him and asked, "The three realms are ablaze;
how can one escape? An took his fire-tongs and pushed the embers aside. As Zhong hesitated, [An struck him].
An said, "Situ, Situ. Zhong suddenly attained realization.
Tao Gu, the Palace Secretary, entered Pujing Monastery in the Eastern Capital to pay his respects to Chan Master Changjue and asked: "The sutras..."
Jiufeng said, "To be free from all marks is what is called 'the Buddhas. Now, before your very eyes, all manner of marks are in disarray; how can you possibly be free from them?
Jue asked, "Attendant, what have you seen? Tao was delighted and looked up to him with great respect.
Prime Minister Li, Prime Minister Li, arrived at Mount Nanyue and questioned Chan Master Shenchen of Fuyan, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master pointed to the cypress tree in front of the courtyard. The Prime Minister asked this three times, and the Master answered him in the same way each time. The Prime Minister was delighted.
Thereupon, a verse says: Appearing and disappearing amidst the leisurely clouds, it fills the great void; Originally, the true mark is not a single speck of dust.
Though asked again and again about the meaning of the Westward Coming, He points only to the single cypress tree in front of the courtyard.
One day, after the Chan Master Qingliang Wenyi had finished discussing the Way with King Li, they went together to view peony flowers.

The King commanded him to compose a verse, and Qingliang immediately composed it, saying: "Clad in coarse wool, facing a fragrant thicket— From the outset, our inclinations have been different. My hair has grown..."
Today’s white flowers were red last year; their lush beauty follows the morning dew, and their fragrance pursues the evening breeze.
What need is there to wait until they wither and fall before one realizes their emptiness? Wang suddenly awakened to the meaning of these words.
Lord Song, Lord Song, served as the Prefect of Hongzhou. One day, a monk from Dajian Temple requested that the second seat be invited to open the hall.
The Lord said, "Why not invite the first seat? The assembly was speechless. (Fayan spoke on their behalf, saying: "There is no need for such trouble.")

Feng Yanshi was the Chancellor of Jiangnan. While traveling with several monks to Mount Zhong, they reached the "Spring for One Person. Feng asked, "How can so many people share this 'Spring for One Person'?
A monk replied, "We simply do not allow it to run dry. Feng Yanshi did not approve of this answer. Thereupon—
Another says: "Who is lacking? (Fayan adds: "Who is it that is insufficient?").
During the Kaibao era, Li Chongju, the Chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was touring and protecting the southern regions. On entering the monastery, he beheld Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva.
Li saw a statue of Kṣitigarbha and asked the monks, "Why does Kṣitigarbha have his hands outstretched? The monks replied, "The jewel in his hand was stolen by a thief.
Li then asked Chan Master Yuanming, "If he is indeed Kṣitigarbha, why did he suffer at the hands of a thief?
Yuanming said, "He has been caught today. Li bowed in gratitude.
Ouyang Xiu, posthumously titled Wenzhong, heard that Chan Master Yuan of Fushan was extraordinary and talented, so he went to his quarters. However, the Master showed no sign of being exceptional.
While Ouyang Xiu was playing chess with guests, Fushan sat beside them. Suddenly, Wenzhong gathered up the chessboard and requested that the Master expound the Dharma based on the game of chess.
Fushan immediately ordered the drum to be beaten. Ascending the seat, he said: "If one discusses this matter, it is like two families playing a game of Go. Why is that?

When facing an opponent who understands the music, one must not yield when the opportunity arises. If one is merely adding five stones to gain three, one must also open up another path before success is achieved.
There is a certain class of people who only know how to secure their own position by closing the gates; they do not understand how to seize the corners or break through the passes. Stubborn!"

The board lines and the tiger’s mouth are aligned; once the position is broken, all efforts at maneuvering are in vain. Thus it is said: "Fat borders are easy to find, but a lean belly is hard to seek.
If one thinks before acting, one often loses the connection; if the mind is coarse, one frequently strikes one's head. Do not boast of being a national master, nor speak in vain of being an immortal.
Setting aside for a moment the question of winning the game or losing the pieces, tell me: when black and white have not yet been distinguished—what then?
"Once you have taken a step, where do you land? After a long silence, he said, "From the beginning, there have been nineteen paths; how many people have been deluded or awakened?
Wen Zhong sighed in admiration and calmly said to his colleagues, "At first, I suspected that Chan discourse was merely empty and exaggerated.

Today, seeing this old man's karmic conditions, I realize that what he has attained and cultivated could not have come about without awakening and clarity within the mind-ground. How could he possibly possess such subtlety otherwise?"

How profound! Later, while serving as an official in Luoyang, he went one day to Mount Song. Leaving his attendants behind, he proceeded with unrestrained ease. Upon reaching a mountain temple, he entered;
the courtyard was filled with tall bamboos, the frost was clear, birds were singing, and the scenery was vividly bright. Wenzhong rested upon the steps of the hall.
Beside him sat an old monk who was reading a scripture with composure. When Wenzhong spoke to him, the monk did not respond with much regard. Wenzhong found this strange.

Wen Zhong asked him, “How long has it been since you, Master, have resided on this mountain? He replied, “It has been very long. Wen Zhong asked again, “What sutra do you recite? He replied, “The Lotus Sutra.
Wen Zhong said, “Among the eminent monks of antiquity, when facing the moment of birth and death, they all for the most part cast off their bodies with talk and laughter.

By what path did they achieve this? He replied, “It was through the power of meditative concentration and wisdom (*samādhi* and *prajñā*). Wen Zhong asked again, “Why is it that nowadays there is none such who remains silent and serene?”
"Why is this? the old monk asked with a smile. "The ancients maintained meditative concentration and wisdom in every thought-moment;
how could they be disturbed at the moment of death? The people of today maintain distraction in every thought-moment; how could they attain stability at the moment of death?
Wen Zhong was so greatly startled that he did not even realize his knees had bent. Xie Xishi once composed a literary record of these events.
Prime Minister Lü Xugong visited the Great Being Fǎhuá Zhìyán and inquired about the essential meaning of the Buddha-dharma. Fǎhuá said:
"Originally there is not a single thing; when the one flavor returns, it becomes true."
King Zhi gathered the Immortal Kings and questioned them: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Fahu replied: "Within the shadows of the green mountains, azure waves surge;
the precious stupa chants aloud, shaking the morning breeze. He further said: "Please, Fahu, burn some incense. Fahu replied: [silence].
He did not seek it through fasting and precepts, nor did he look for it from the Buddha.
Xu Yue, Assistant Lecturer at the National Academy, asked about the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West. Fǎhuá said: "The one on the eastern side of the street."
Xu said, "I have not yet understood. Fahua said, "Three kinds of people cannot understand it.
Wang Anshi, Wang Anshi—his courtesy name was Jiefu. He served as Prime Minister under Emperor Renzong and was enfeoffed as Duke of Jing. At that time, Chan Master Wushan Duan was at [the monastery]."
In the capital, the Duke requested that [Zhao]duan lecture on Chan. A vegetarian feast was prepared at the Great Xiangguo Monastery.
After the Duke had entered the hall and finished burning incense, he asked the assembly, "What sutra did one study before the Buddha appeared in the world? The assembly remained silent.
Zhao Duan said, "Duke, what books were read before Zhou Gong and Confucius appeared in the world? The Duke replied, "A clever monk. Zhao Duan then spoke this verse: South...
"Avalokiteśvara does not appear; he speaks various dharmas. The ocean of sentient beings' karma is deep, and thus they are difficult to rescue.

Those who have sunk throughout past and present cry out in lamentation for the Bodhisattva at every sound. At that time, the Duke was in court, renewing the affairs of state, and thus composed this verse.
Whenever the Duke saw the verses of Duan, he would praise them, saying, "One who has the fundamental source is like this. (Hong Juefan said:)

When Lord Wang Wen was about to receive the great appointment, guests seeking congratulations crowded his gate. The Lord sat in silence for a very long time, then suddenly inscribed upon the wall: "The frost-battered bamboo and snow-covered bamboo at Zhongshan Temple; I shall retire there in my old age to spend the rest of my life. Later, during the Lantern Festival, he was granted a banquet at Xiangguo Temple where he watched acrobatic performers.

The guests were exceedingly joyful, but the Lord composed a verse: "Among the performers on the stage, one is noble and another is lowly; yet I know in my heart they are fundamentally the same, and thus I feel neither joy nor resentment. He once said to his fellow students: "This old man has eyes all over his body; there is not a single spot that does not see. (He was so perceptive that there was not a single point where he lacked insight.)
The layman Liu of Wuchang and the elder Shun of Yunju first studied under Dongshan. One day, while traveling through Wuchang to beg for alms, Shun went first to visit Layman Liu.
The Layman said, "I have a question for you, old man. If our views accord, I shall invite you to open the sutras; if they do not accord—"
He immediately invited [Zhaozhou] to return to the mountain. He then asked, "How was it before the ancient mirror had been polished?
Zhaozhou said, "Black as lacquer. "How is it after it has been polished? Zhaozhou said, "It reflects heaven and reflects earth.

The layman gave a long bow and said, "Please, Master, return to the mountain. Zhaozhou returned home feeling somewhat abashed. Dongshan asked him the reason for this, and Zhaozhou recounted his previous words. Dongshan said, "Ask me about it. Zhaozhou did so.
Dongshan replied to the former question, "It is not far from here to Hanyang. To the latter remark, Dongshan said, "Before the Yellow Crane Tower is Parrot Isle.
At these words, Shun attained great enlightenment.
The Layman Li Duanyuan was renowned in his time for his Buddhist studies. Zen Master Zongben of Huelin asked him, "The ten directions gather together;
each and every one studies non-action (*wuwei*). Now, since it is called 'non-action,' how does one study it? Li had no reply.

Ye Qingchen, the Vice Director of the Imperial Chancellery, while serving as Governor of Jinling, went to welcome Chan Master Weizheng to discuss the Way. One day, Ye said, "Tomorrow there is a banquet at the Prefecture.
Although you, Master, strictly observe the monastic precepts, could you stay for one more day to accept my invitation for conversation?"
He accepted the invitation. The following day, a messenger was sent to invite him; however, Zhen left behind a verse and departed, saying: "Yesterday I made plans for today;
Leaving the gate, leaning on my staff, I reflected again: As a monk, it is fitting to dwell among crags and valleys;

At a banquet for a state guest, this is truly inappropriate. The guests present all admired his refined character. Imperial Commissioner of Hangzhou, Vice Minister Jiang, also became a fellow practitioner with Zhen.

Regarding his diplomatic visits: whenever he went to pay his respects, he would unyoke his oxen at the foot of the prefectural courtyard and depart after spending the entire day in conversation and laughter.
Jiang composed a poem about him which says: "The Zen guest regularly enters the old capital; A flask and bowl hang from the horns of a yellow ox. Sometimes he goes through clouds and snow;
It would be well to paint him together with the clouds."
Chen Guan, whose courtesy name was Tuifu, once asked Zongdao before entering the provincial examination hall, "I wish to become the Grand Marshal (Zhuangyuan) on this journey;
do you think I can? Zongdao looked at him intently and replied, "It will not happen. Tuifu ultimately ranked third.
At that time, the leader was the official Yan. Chen Liangbi,
the Grand Marshal (Taishou) of Song,
who held the rank of Grand Marshal (Taiwei), invited Neten Yuanwu Fazhen, Cishou, and ten eminent Dharma masters.
A thousand monks from the Chan and Lecture schools were attending a state banquet in the capital. At that time, Emperor Huizong went there in private to observe the proceedings;

the Grand Astrologer, Duke of Lu, was also present. There was a man named Shanhua, who was a "tiger among scholars" of the Xianshou (Huayan) school. He addressed the assembly and questioned the Chan masters, saying:
"In the teachings established by our Buddha, from the Hinayana up to the Perfect and Sudden [teachings], he has swept away both emptiness and existence, leaving only..."
Only after realizing the true and eternal, and being subsequently adorned with the myriad virtues, can one be called a Buddha.
I have heard it said that a single shout of the Chan school can transform an ordinary person into a sage; this seems to contradict the various sutras and treatises.

Now, if a single shout can enter the five teachings of our school, it constitutes the correct teaching; if it cannot so enter, it is a false teaching. This is the view of the Pure Cause School of Chan.
Jingyin said, "Regarding what the Dharma Master has asked, it is insufficient for the great Chan masters to provide a full response.
I, Jingyin, a minor elder, can ensure that the Dharma Master is free from doubt. Jingyin summoned Shan; Shan responded with an assent.
Jingyin said, "What the Dharma Master calls the 'Hīnayāna teachings of the foolish' possess existence as their meaning. What is called the 'Initial Teaching of the Mahāyāna' is emptiness."
This is the meaning. The Mahāyāna Final Teaching (Zhòngjiào) is the principle of neither being nor non-being. The Mahāyāna Sudden Teaching (Dùnjiào) is the principle of being-while-being-empty.
The One Vehicle Perfect Teaching (Yīshèng Yuánjiào) is the principle of being while not being, and being empty while not being empty.
Just as my single shout is not only able to penetrate these five teachings, it even extends to the arts and crafts and the various branches of learning.
"Of all the hundred schools, you are able to enter them all. Jingyin then let out a thunderous shout and asked, "Did you hear it?
Shanshan replied, "I heard it. Jingyin said, "Since you heard it, this shout just now exists; you have been able to enter the teachings of the Hīnayāna.
A moment later, he asked Shanshan again, "Did you hear it? He replied, "I did not hear it. Jingyin said, "Since you did not hear it, that previous shout was non-existent."

He was able to enter the Initial Teaching (Shijiao). He then turned to Shan and said: "When I first let out a shout, you said it 'exists. When the shout has long since faded and the sound has vanished, you say it 'does not exist.
To say it does not exist implies that it originally truly existed; to say it exists implies that it currently truly does not exist.

Being neither existent nor non-existent, one can enter the Final Teaching (Zhongjiao). At the time I have the shout, existence is not existence, for existence arises because of non-existence. Non-existence...

At the moment of this shout, there is nothing that is not non-existence; because existence exists, there is non-existence. Existence and non-existence are simultaneous. One can thus enter the Sudden Teaching.

You must know that this one shout of mine does not function as a mere shout; it transcends both existence and non-existence, and both intellectual understanding and emotional attachments are forgotten.

When the Way is spoken of as existing, not even a speck of dust is established; when the Way is spoken of as non-existent, it extends horizontally throughout empty space. Through this very shout, one enters the hundred [teachings].
Ten million billion shouts, a hundred thousand ten million billion shouts—all enter into this single shout. Therefore, one is able to enter the Perfect Teaching (*yuanjiao*).
Shan then rose and bowed twice. Jingyin spoke again, saying: "It is not only this single shout that is thus.

Even down to a single word and a single silence, a single movement and a single stillness—from antiquity to the present, throughout the empty space of the ten directions, and within the myriad phenomena of the six paths and four births—"

The Buddhas of the three periods of time, all the sages and worthies, the eighty-four thousand Dharma-gates, the hundreds of thousands of samādhis, and the immeasurable subtle meanings—all of which accord with principle and adapt to capacity, and are of one substance with heaven, earth, and the myriad things—are called the *dharmakāya*.

That the three realms are mind-only and the myriad dharmas are consciousness-only, and that the four seasons and eight nodes of the calendar are of one essence with the yin and yang, is called the *dharmatā*. Therefore:
The *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* states: "The Dharma-nature pervades all places—whether with form or without form, whether a single sound or a single color.
Within a single mote of dust, it fully contains four meanings; phenomena and principle are boundless, pervasive without exception.

They interpenetrate without being confused, and they blend without becoming one. All of these are fully present within this single shout. This is still the gate of provisional manifestation, responding to capacities."
"Expedient means" refers to what is called a temporary resting place; one has not yet reached the place of treasure.

Little do they realize that within the gate of our ancestral masters, there is the transmission of mind through mind and the sealing of dharma through dharma. It does not rely on words and letters; it is to see one's nature and become a Buddha.
There exists a supreme path that has not been transmitted by a thousand sages. Shan asked again, "What is this supreme path? Jingyin replied:
“You should go down and understand it for yourself. Shàn said, “What is the treasure-place? Jìngyīn said, “It is not within your realm.
Shàn said, “I look to the Chan Master’s compassion. Jìngyīn said, “Even if the vast ocean were to change, I would never explain it for you.”
He skillfully concluded his discourse and withdrew; those who heard him could not help but admire and look up to him in awe.

The Emperor turned to his attendants and said, "The profound mystery of the Chan school reaches such depths, and Jingyin’s talent and eloquence are likewise rare. An attendant replied, "This is but the overflow of the Master’s teachings."
Li Chaqing, together with his nephew, the lay practitioner Xianglin Jushi Xiang Ziyin, visited Chan Master Lin of Daochang.
They then asked, "When the household thief harasses one, what then? Lin said, "Who is the household thief? Li raised his fist. Lin said, "The thief!"
His body was already exposed. Li said, "Do not try to deceive people. Lin said, "The evidence is right here. Li was speechless.
Qian Xiangzu—his courtesy name was Gongxiang—was a native of Qiantang. While serving as the Governor of Jinling during the reign of Emperor Ningzong, he once sought the Way from [Linji].
Chan Master Wuyong of Baoning again sought the Way from Chan Master Yuan of Huguosi, Chican.

Chican said, "If you wish to investigate this matter, you must reach the point where both mind and dharmas are forgotten. If attachment to dharmas (*dharmagrāha*) has not been forgotten, then even if you accord with the principle, it is not yet awakening.
Baoning asked, "If one merely engages the lips and tongue, one immediately falls into mental fabrication (*manas*); how can this be? Chican replied, "It is fundamentally non-existent."

"Do not wound the sore. The Duke was suddenly enlightened and attained realization. He had previously established ten reception centers throughout his home province, all of which he named after the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*).
He also founded the Upper Hermitage and a residence for eminent monks as places for discussing the Way.

After resigning from the position of Left Minister and returning home, he devoted himself even more to the practice of the Pure Land. Once, when he suffered a slight illness, a monk came to inquire after his health, and the Duke said: "No..."
"Born of greed, one does not fear death. One will not be born as a deva nor as a human; one shall only be reborn in the Pure Land.
Having spoken these words, he sat in the full lotus posture and passed away. *Qianjue zongcheng*, Scroll Four. Recorded by Shidun Yangtonrang of Shuangji.
The Patriarchal Vehicle of the First Awakened Ones, Volume Five.
Edited by the Elder Yufeng of Mount Jing, Yuanxin;
collated by Gudizhu Ren, Guo Ningzhi. Compiled.
The Censor-in-Chief of Hongzhou—his name has been lost—asked Mazu, "Is it right to eat wine and meat, or is it not?
Mazu replied, "If you eat them, it is the official emolument of a censor; if you do not eat them, it is the merit of a censor. The Censor-in-Chief attained realization.
A Layman Asks about Heaven and Hell:
A certain layman asked Zen Master Xitang Zhizang, "Are there heavens and hells? The Master replied, "There are."
[The monk] asked, "Are there not the Treasures of Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha? The Master said, "There are. [The monk] asked further questions, and to all of them the Master replied, "There are.
[The monk] said, "When you, Reverend, speak in this way, are you not mistaken? The Master said, "Have you ever met a venerable elder?
[The monk] said, "I have previously attended upon the Reverend of Mount Jing. The Master said, "How did he speak to you? [The monk] said, "He spoke of 'One'."
[The monk] replied, "Completely none. The Master asked, "Do you have a wife? He replied, "I do. The Master said, "Does the Abbot of Jingshan have a wife?
He replied, "He does not. The Master said, "The Abbot of Jingshan may indeed say he has none."
Guizong was asked by an official about Chan Master Zhichang of Guizong on Mount Lu. Because the official had come, Guizong picked up the two straps of his hat and said, "Do you understand?
The official replied, "I do not understand. Guizong said, "Do not blame the old monk for his headache; I will not take off my hat."

A Confucian asked, "There is a Confucian among the three teachings, but I have forgotten his name. He then asked Chan Master Dazhu Hai, "Regarding the three teachings of Confucianism, Buddhism, and Daoism, how do their similarities and differences compare?
The Master said, "For those of great capacity, they function as one; for those of limited faculties, they are grasped as different. In total, they all derive from the One."

The functioning of the arising of nature (xingqi) manifests as three distinctions according to the differences in the capacities of those who perceive it; delusion and enlightenment depend on the person, not on whether the teaching is the same or different.
When a practitioner asked, "Regarding 'this very mind is Buddha,' what is that Buddha? Dazhu replied, "You have doubts."
"That is not the Buddha. Point it out! When the practitioner had no reply, Dazhu said: "To realize it is for everything to be the realm;
failing to awaken is to remain forever alienated."

A layman asked Zen Master Jing.
The layman’s name is unknown. He addressed Zen Master Jing, saying, "Whenever I sit in meditation at night, my thoughts fly about in confusion.
I do not yet understand the method for subduing them; I pray that you will deign to instruct me. The Master said, "If, during the night, you sit in tranquility..."
The mind’s thoughts fly about in confusion. Take this confused and flying mind and investigate the place from which it flies.

When you investigate and find no such place, then where do these confused thoughts exist? Turn back and investigate the investigating mind itself; then where is the mind that is capable of investigating?

Furthermore, the wisdom that can illuminate is fundamentally empty, and the objects illuminated are likewise quiescent. This quiescence is not merely quiescent, for there is nothing that can be made quiescent.

Such a person is one who illuminates yet does not illuminate; this is because there is no objective realm to be illuminated. When both realm and wisdom are quiescent, the mind and its deliberations are at peace.
One does not seek out branches externally, nor does one dwell in meditative concentration internally. When these two paths are both obliterated, the single nature is serene.
This is the essential path for returning to the source.

The Minister said, "The Buddhas and Patriarchs were at a loss for words; you have pointed out the source of delusion and killed countless people.
Yangqi said, "Why did you rob me right where I stood? The Minister replied, "It turns out you are actually one of my own family. Yangqi laughed heartily. The Minister also laughed.
A layman went to the Fifth Patriarch to leave the household life.

Another layman also went to the Fifth Patriarch to leave the household life and said, "I am renouncing my worldly conditions. The Fifth Patriarch asked, "What do you mean by 'renouncing worldly conditions'?"
The scholar said, "To abandon one's wife and children is called 'abandoning conditions. The Fifth Patriarch said, "I too have a wife;
do you believe me? The scholar remained silent. The Fifth Patriarch then uttered this verse: "I have a wife, Whom no one in the world has seen.
Day and night we dwell together, Naturally possessing skillful means."
A Layman Visits Wuzu to Offer Food to the Monks.
There was a layman in Shuzhou who regularly went to Wuzu to provide meals for the monks. One day he asked the Head Seat, "I am a worldly person;
can I practice Chan? The Head Seat replied, "You are a worldly person; how could you practice Chan? The layman did not...
He brought this up for the Fifth Patriarch, who said, "The Head Seat indeed possesses the authentic means to benefit others.
Only then did the layman believe, whereupon he became resolute in his investigation. Later, he met Foyan, who extended his hand and asked, "Why do you call this a hand?
At that moment, the layman suddenly attained great enlightenment.

A Layman Questions Yunfeng Yue: A layman asked Chan Master Yunfeng Wenyue, "What is the Buddha? Yunfeng said, "Dress, eat, and manage your household affairs. The layman said, "If that is so, then I shall step back three paces and join my palms at my chest. Yunfeng said, "Go ahead. The layman did as he was told. Yunfeng said, "Now, what is the Buddha? The layman said, "I do not know. Yunfeng said, "You do not even know your own head; how can you possibly know the Buddha? The layman said, "I have come from afar to seek the Dharma; why do you strike me with such words? Yunfeng said, "Because you do not know your own head. The layman said, "How can one know one's own head? Yunfeng said, "When you put on clothes and eat food, you naturally know hunger and cold; this is your head. The layman said, "If that is so, then I am indeed the Buddha. Yunfeng said, "If you are the Buddha, then you must be able to save sentient beings. The layman said, "I am already saving them. Yunfeng said, "Who are you saving? The layman said, "The hungry, I feed; the cold, I warm; the suffering, I relieve. Yunfeng said, "If you are truly the Buddha, you should be able to manifest transformations. The layman said, "I will transform for you. Yunfeng said, "Transform yourself into a dog. The layman immediately transformed into a dog and went out the gate. Yunfeng called out, "Dog! The dog barked three times and returned. Yunfeng said, "This is merely a dog; where is the Buddha? The layman said, "I have already shown you the Buddha; why do you still ask? Yunfeng said, "You have shown me the dog, but you have not shown me the Buddha. The layman said, "I have shown you both the dog and the Buddha. Yunfeng said, "Where is the Buddha? The layman pointed to the dog. Yunfeng said, "This is the dog; where is the Buddha? The layman said, "The Buddha is right here. Yunfeng said, "If you are the Buddha, you should be able to fly. The layman immediately flew up into the air. Yunfeng said, "This is merely a bird; where is the Buddha? The layman said, "I have already shown you the Buddha; why do you still ask? Yunfeng said, "You have shown me the bird, but you have not shown me the Buddha. The layman said, "I have shown you both the bird and the Buddha. Yunfeng said, "Where is the Buddha? The layman pointed to the bird. Yunfeng said, "This is the bird; where is the Buddha? The layman said, "The Buddha is right here. Yunfeng said, "If you are the Buddha, you should be able to pass through walls. The layman immediately passed through the wall. Yunfeng said, "This is merely a ghost; where is the Buddha? The layman said, "I have already shown you the Buddha; why do you still ask? Yunfeng said, "You have shown me the ghost, but you have not shown me the Buddha. The layman said, "I have shown you both the ghost and the Buddha. Yunfeng said, "Where is the Buddha? The layman pointed to the ghost. Yunfeng said, "This is the ghost; where is the Buddha? The layman said, "The Buddha is right here. Yunfeng said, "If you are the Buddha, you should be able to enter the water without getting wet. The layman immediately entered the pond and emerged dry. Yunfeng said, "This is merely a fish; where is the Buddha? The layman said, "I have already shown you the Buddha; why do you still ask? Yunfeng said, "You have shown me the fish, but you have not shown me the Buddha. The layman said, "I have shown you both the fish and the Buddha. Yunfeng said, "Where is the Buddha? The layman pointed to the fish. Yunfeng said, "This is the fish; where is the Buddha? The layman said, "The Buddha is right here. Yunfeng said, "If you are the Buddha, you should be able to ascend to the heavens. The layman immediately ascended into the sky. Yunfeng said, "This is merely a star; where is the Buddha? The layman said, "I have already shown you the Buddha; why do you still ask? Yunfeng said, "You have shown me the star, but you have not shown me the Buddha. The layman said, "I have shown you both the star and the Buddha. Yunfeng said, "Where is the Buddha? The layman pointed to the star. Yunfeng said, "This is the star; where is the Buddha? The layman said, "The Buddha is right here. Yunfeng said, "If you are the Buddha, you should be able to enter fire without being burned. The layman immediately entered a blazing furnace and emerged unscathed. Yunfeng said, "This is merely a flame; where is the Buddha? The layman said, "I have already shown you the Buddha; why do you still ask? Yunfeng said, "You have shown me the flame, but you have not shown me the Buddha. The layman said, "I have shown you both the flame and the Buddha. Yunfeng said, "Where is the Buddha? The layman pointed to the flame. Yunfeng said, "This is the flame; where is the Buddha? The layman said, "The Buddha is right here. Yunfeng said, "If you are the Buddha, you should be able to vanish into emptiness. The layman immediately vanished. Yunfeng said, "This is merely nothingness; where is the Buddha? The layman said, "I have already shown you the Buddha; why do you still ask? Yunfeng said, "You have shown me nothingness, but you have not shown me the Buddha. The layman said, "I have shown you both nothingness and the Buddha. Yunfeng said, "Where is the Buddha? The layman pointed to nothingness. Yunfeng said, "This is nothingness; where is the Buddha? The layman said, "The Buddha is right here. Yunfeng said, "If you are the Buddha, you should be able to hear sounds without ears. The layman said, "I have no ears. Yunfeng said, "Since you have no ears, how can you hear? The layman said, "Hearing is precisely because there are no ears. Yunfeng said, "If you have no ears, how can you speak? The layman said, "Speaking is precisely because there are no ears. Yunfeng said, "If you have no ears, how can you see? The layman said, "Seeing is precisely because there are no ears. Yunfeng said, "If you have no ears, how can you smell? Feng said, "It is better to have no cup at all than to add another after one is drunk.
When Governor Lü Gong asked about Jiuding,
he went to visit the Great Image and questioned the Chan Master Qingsu of Jiuding, saying, "Since this is a great image, for what purpose..."
"What is it that bears the two pillars? Jiuding replied, "There are no idle hands on a boat.

Arriving below the pavilion, he beheld the Avalokiteśvara image and asked again, "The realm of Maitreya—whence does Avalokiteśvara come? Jiuding said, "When a family is wealthy, the children are spoiled;
the Governor has merely paid him homage."
The Minister asked Chan Master Faqing of Jiuxian, "Where is your native place, Senior? He replied, "Yanzhou.
The Minister said, "Is that the same as this place, or is it different? Jiuxian pulled down his *kāṣāya* to the ground, bowed, and said, "Official."
"Have you ever been to Yanzhou? Ceng was at a loss for words. Jiuxian said, "When you, Official, arrive in Yanzhou, then tell the Official:
'In Yizhou, I took my leave of the Prefect.'"
When Chan Master Chengyuan of Yizhou was about to pass away, he took his leave of the Prefect, saying, "I, this old monk, am going on a pilgrimage.
The Vice-Prefect remarked, "This monk is mad; at eighty years of age, where would he go on a pilgrimage? The Prefect replied, "He is a great spiritual teacher (mahā-upādhyāya)."
Moving and staying at will, the patrol inspector questioned Huanglong Ming.
Huanglong, together with Inspector Hu, went to Ersheng Temple in Gong’an. The inspector asked, "When Bodhidharma faced Emperor Wu of Liang..."
The Emperor said, "Vast and empty, there is no sage. Master An, why then do you have two sages?
Huanglong said, "A single drop of ink forms two dragons."
A layman asked Master Guiren:
"Can an ordinary person still be permitted to understand the Buddha-dharma? Guiren replied:
"Which terrace is without the moon? Whose tree does not flower in spring?"
An official asked Master Qingpou of Xingyang, "When will you open the hall for teaching? The Master said:
Without passing through the countless *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, before the sun and moon were born.
A layman asked Master Tianping:
"A layman asked Master Tianping Qiyu, 'How is it when there is no movement or fluctuation in the Dharma? Tianping—
Tianping asked, "You have come from Lufu. The layman replied, "I have not taken a single step. Tianping asked, "How did you get here?
The layman said, "Why do you speak in your sleep, Monk? Tianping said, "I grant you twenty blows.
Then another official asked, "When there are no neighbors to separate one from another, why do we not see each other? Tianping said, "It is a grievance!"
Who? A layman asked Master Dongshan Yungding of Fuzhou. A layman asked, saying: "Dongshan said there is 'one thing' that..."
“It supports the heavens above and the earth below. I wonder what kind of thing this is? The Master said, “Carrying an iron cangue and receiving iron blows.
[The student] said, “Heaven and earth turn black; mountains and rivers flee. The Master said, “One more ghost is added before the Hall of Lord Yama;
he lies for a thousand years beneath Mount Beimang. The student cried out, “What joy! What joy! The Master said, “This too is just a wild fox swallowing a mouse.”
A young boy was carrying a scripture on his head. When it was the turn for another boy to carry the scripture, the monk ordered him to place the scripture inside a case.
The boy said, "The one I am reciting—where should that be placed? (Fayan spoke on his behalf: "What scripture are you reciting?")
At Hongtang Bridge, an official asked a monk, "On this Hongtang Bridge in Fuzhou, there are monks sitting in rows. Is there a Buddha among them?
The monk had no reply. (Fayan spoke on his behalf, saying: "Who are you?")
The Salt Seller:
Once there was a monk traveling to Fushan who encountered a salt seller on the road. The monk asked, "Where does the road to Fushan lead?
The man remained silent for a long time. The monk asked again, whereupon the man said, "Are you deaf? The monk replied, "Are you speaking to me?"
"What do you say? The old man replied, "I tell you, it is the Road of the Overturned Boat. The monk asked, "Do you not understand Zen?
The old man said, "Let alone understanding Zen; I have mastered all of the Buddha-dharma as well. The monk said, "Try explaining it for me. The old man lifted up his salt basket.
The monk said, "Difficult. The old man asked, "What do you call this? The monk said, "Salt. The old man said, "What connection is there?
The monk asked, "What do you call it? [The old man] said, "I cannot tell you again that it is salt."
The Monk Gōngqī, known as the "Young Master Riding an Ox," was traveling toward Luóhàn when he encountered a young master riding an ox along the way.
The Master asked, "Which way does the road to Luóhàn go? The young master slapped the ox and said, "Speak! Speak! The Master shouted, "You beast! The young master replied, "Luóhàn..."
"Where does the Han road lead? The Master then patted the ox and said, "Speak! Speak!
The official said, "Even if it were so, there would still be hooves and horns missing. The Master struck him. The official patted the ox and ran away.
The Man on the Donkey.
Long ago, there was a man riding a donkey who asked the assembly of monks, "Where are you going? The monks replied, "To the site of enlightenment (the *bodhimaṇḍa*).
The man said, "Where is it that this is not the site of enlightenment? The monks beat him, saying, "This fellow has no sense! He rides his donkey right upon the site of enlightenment!"

In the Buddha hall, a hawk was chasing a pigeon. The pigeon flew toward the railing of the Buddha hall and trembled.
Someone asked a monk, "All sentient beings dwell in constant peace and joy within the shadow of the Buddha. Why does this pigeon tremble upon seeing the Buddha? The monk had no reply.
Regarding this (Dafeng [Daichun] says: "I fear the Buddha"), the Prince of Guangnan went out hunting.
There was a monk living in a hermitage there. When the Prince went out hunting, his attendants informed the master of the hermitage, saying, "The Great King is coming; please rise."
The abbot said, "It is not only when the Great King comes that I do not rise; even if the Buddha were to come, I would still not rise.

The King asked, "Is the Buddha not your teacher? The abbot replied, "He is. The King said, "If so, why do you not rise upon seeing your teacher? (Fayan spoke on his behalf, saying: "This does not yet suffice to repay his kindness.")
An Official Enters the Tianwang Temple in Zhenzhou.
Formerly, there was an official who entered the Tianwang Temple in Zhenzhou and, beholding the divine image, asked the temple master, "What meritorious deed is this?
He replied, "It is the Guardian King of the State. The official asked, "Does he protect only this country, or does he protect all other countries as well? The master replied, "He dwells here..."
"Qin is Qin; Chu is Chu. [The monk] said, "On the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth month, they broke down the city walls of Zhenzhou.
Where has the Heavenly King gone? The Abbot had no reply. (Miyun Wu said: "Gentlemen, do not plot rebellion! He further said: 'Today I have obtained the gentlemen as witnesses.'"")
The Official’s Treatise on the Non-existence of Ghosts:

Long ago, there was an official who composed a treatise titled "On the Non-existence of Ghosts. One night, while he was wielding his brush in the middle of the night, he suddenly saw a ghost appear and say, "You claim there are no ghosts;
what about me? (Wuzu Yan said: "If I had been there at that time, I would have made the gesture of a magpie's beak with my hand and said to him, 'Gu-gu-ku! [a sound made by a magpie]).
The official asked, “What is the name of the monk who makes no distinctions? He replied, “No distinctions. The official said, “If someone were suddenly to offer you a bowl of sand, what would you do?
He replied, “I thank the official for his offering. (Fayan commented separately: “This is still a case of making distinctions.”)
